mainTopic: מַעְשַׂר בְּהֵמָה: where it applies, רבי עקיבא's view, and why it is not practiced nowadays
overview: A new פרק opens with a משנה about מעשר בהמה. It applies in ארץ ישראל and in חוץ לארץ, with or without the בית המקדש, and only to חולין. The משנה also rules that cattle and flock animals are counted separately, and so are animals from different years. Sheep and goats are counted together, because the פסוק calls them all צאן. The גמרא first asks whether the משנה contradicts רבי עקיבא, who links מעשר בהמה to מעשר דגן. It answers that רבי עקיבא only means the animal from חוץ לארץ is not brought as a sacrifice. The animal still becomes holy, so the owner may eat it only once it has a מום. Next the גמרא asks why we do not tithe animals today. רב הונא's reason, a decree because of an orphan animal, is rejected. רבה explains instead that the concern is a תקלה, the misuse of a holy animal, and he proves it from a ברייתא that forbids consecrating anything nowadays. The amud ends with a challenge: by that logic, firstborn animals should be prevented from becoming holy by selling part of them to a non-Jew.

steps.title: Where and when animal tithe applies
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that מעשר בהמה applies in and outside ארץ ישראל, with or without the בית המקדש, but only to חולין.
steps.simpleTranslation: MISHNA: Animal tithe applies in the Land and outside the Land, while the Temple stands and when it does not, to non-sacred animals but not to consecrated animals.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה opens the chapter by telling us the basic reach of the מצוה of מעשר בהמה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Three limits are set out. Location does not matter, since the מצוה applies in ארץ ישראל and in חוץ לארץ. Time does not matter, since it applies with or without the בית המקדש. The status of the animal does matter: only חולין are tithed, not animals already consecrated as קדשים.

keyTerms.meaning: Animal tithe: every tenth animal born in the herd or flock becomes holy.
In the time the Temple stands.
Animals already consecrated to the Temple.

steps.whyThisMatters: The ruling that the מצוה applies in חוץ לארץ is exactly what the גמרא will question in light of רבי עקיבא.

phrases.english: MISHNA: Animal tithe
applies in the Land and outside the Land,
while the Temple stands and when the Temple does not stand,
to non-sacred animals but not to consecrated animals.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַעְשַׂר בְּהֵמָה נוֹהֵג בָּאָרֶץ וּבְחוּצָה לָאָרֶץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opening of a new perek.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מעשר בהמה applies everywhere and at all times, but only to חולין.

steps.title: Which animal kinds may be tithed together
steps.stepSummary: Cattle and flock animals are each tithed, but not one for the other. Sheep and goats may be tithed one for the other.
steps.simpleTranslation: It applies to cattle and to flock animals, but they are not tithed from one for the other. It applies to sheep and goats, and they are tithed from one for the other.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה explains which animals may be counted together in one group of ten.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "Tithed from one for the other" means counting them together, so the tenth animal covers both kinds. Cattle (בקר) and flock animals (צאן) must be counted separately. Sheep and goats, which are both types of צאן, are counted together.

keyTerms.meaning: Tithed from one for the other, meaning counted together.

phrases.english: And it applies to cattle and to flock animals,
but they are not tithed from one for the other.
It applies to sheep and to goats,
and they are tithed from one for the other.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה with rules about combining animals.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בקר and צאן are counted separately. Sheep and goats are counted together.

steps.title: New-year and old-year animals are counted separately
steps.stepSummary: Animals born in different tithe years are each tithed, but they cannot be counted together.
steps.simpleTranslation: It applies to new and to old animals, but they are not tithed from one for the other.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds that animals from a new year and animals from an old year may not be combined.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "New" and "old" refer to animals born in different tithing years. Even though they are the same species, each year's animals must be tithed on their own. This rule becomes the starting point for the reasoning in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: New: animals born in the current tithe year.
Old: animals born in the previous tithe year.

phrases.english: It applies to the new and to the old,
but they are not tithed from one for the other.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another combining rule, this time based on time rather than species.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Animals from different tithe years are not counted together.

steps.title: Logic would suggest sheep and goats should not combine
steps.stepSummary: The משנה raises a קל וחומר. If new and old animals, which are not כלאים, do not combine, then sheep and goats, which are כלאים, should certainly not combine.
steps.simpleTranslation: For it would have been logical: if new and old animals, which are not forbidden mixtures with each other, are not tithed one for the other, then sheep and goats, which are forbidden mixtures with each other, should surely not be tithed one for the other.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה builds an argument that seems to contradict its own rule about sheep and goats. This sets up the next step, where a פסוק overrides the argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: New and old animals are so similar that mating them is not כלאים, yet they still may not be combined. Sheep and goats are different enough that mating them is כלאים. By קל וחומר, they should be even less able to combine.

keyTerms.meaning: For it would have been logical.
If even, the opening formula of a קל וחומר.
Forbidden mixtures, such as cross-breeding different species.

steps.confusionAlert: This is not the final ruling. The argument is raised only so that it can be rejected by the פסוק in the next step. Sheep and goats do combine.

phrases.english: For it would have been logical:
if the new and the old,
which are not forbidden mixtures with each other,
are not tithed from one for the other,
then sheep and goats,
which are forbidden mixtures with each other,

phrases.aramaic: אֵינוֹ דִּין שֶׁלֹּא יְהוּ מִתְעַשְּׂרִין מִזֶּה עַל זֶה?
phrases.english: is it not logical that they should not be tithed from one for the other?

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁהָיָה בַּדִּין, וּמָה אִם הֶחָדָשׁ וְהַיָּשָׁן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the new/old rule from step 3 to challenge the sheep/goats rule from step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that sheep and goats are tithed together.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A קל וחומר from new and old animals, which do not combine even though they are not כלאים.

steps.title: The verse makes all flock animals one group
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק "וצאן" teaches that all flock animals count as one group for the tithe.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says "or the flock," which implies that all flock animals are one.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה answers the logical argument with a פסוק that groups sheep and goats together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah uses the single word צאן, which covers both sheep and goats. That shows they are one category for מעשר בהמה. An explicit פסוק overrides the קל וחומר.
steps.whatToRemember: Sheep and goats are counted together for מעשר בהמה because the Torah calls them all צאן, even though logic alone might have kept them apart.

phrases.english: The verse says: "or the flock,"
implying that all flock animals are one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Overrides the קל וחומר of step 4.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Sheep and goats should not combine because they are כלאים.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק defines all צאן as one group, so they combine.

steps.title: Does the משנה contradict רבי עקיבא?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that our משנה does not follow רבי עקיבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: GEMARA: Shall we say that our משנה is not in accordance with רבי עקיבא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by suggesting the משנה conflicts with רבי עקיבא. This sets up the ברייתא it is about to quote.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The target is the משנה's rule that מעשר בהמה applies even in חוץ לארץ. The גמרא hints that רבי עקיבא holds otherwise, and the proof comes next.

phrases.english: GEMARA: Shall we say that our Mishnah
is not in accordance with Rabbi Akiva?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns to analyze the first clause of the משנה (step 1).
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's rule that מעשר בהמה applies in חוץ לארץ.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: It seems to contradict the opinion of רבי עקיבא.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא's ברייתא: the question and the verse
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא. רבי עקיבא asks whether animal tithe from חוץ לארץ should be brought and sacrificed, and cites a פסוק listing "your tithes."
steps.simpleTranslation: For it was taught: רבי עקיבא says, one might think a person should bring up animal tithe from outside the Land and sacrifice it. The verse says: "And you shall bring there your burnt offerings, and your sacrifices, and your tithes."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source behind its suggestion. רבי עקיבא raises a possible mistake and quotes a פסוק to address it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא first suggests that animal tithe from חוץ לארץ might be brought to the בית המקדש. The פסוק it cites uses the plural "your tithes," and the next step explains how that plural answers the question.

phrases.english: As it was taught: Rabbi Akiva says:
One might think that a person should bring up
animal tithe from outside the Land
and sacrifice it?
The verse says:
"And you shall bring there your burnt offerings,
and your sacrifices, and your tithes."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Provides the source behind the challenge of step 6.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי עקיבא disagrees with the משנה about חוץ לארץ.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא quoting רבי עקיבא's reading of the פסוק in דברים.

steps.title: Animal tithe is linked to grain tithe
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא explains that "tithes" refers to two tithes. Animal tithe is brought only from where grain tithe is brought, which is ארץ ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse speaks of two tithes, animal tithe and grain tithe. From the place where you bring up grain tithe, you bring up animal tithe. From a place where you do not bring up grain tithe, you do not bring up animal tithe.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא finishes his derivation by tying מעשר בהמה to מעשר דגן. The גמרא treats this as clashing with the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מעשר דגן applies only in ארץ ישראל. Since the פסוק groups both tithes in one word, animal tithe is brought only from where grain tithe is brought, which is ארץ ישראל. The גמרא understands this to mean that רבי עקיבא excludes חוץ לארץ, while the משנה includes it.

keyTerms.meaning: Tithe of grain (produce), meaning מעשר שני.

steps.confusionAlert: רבי עקיבא's words are about bringing (מעלה) the tithe to the בית המקדש. Whether they also mean there is no obligation at all in חוץ לארץ is exactly what the גמרא's challenge assumes. Step 9 answers this by separating offering the animal from its becoming holy.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the central tension of the סוגיא: how the משנה's ruling for חוץ לארץ fits with רבי עקיבא.

phrases.english: The verse is speaking of two tithes:

phrases.aramaic: אֶחָד מַעְשַׂר בְּהֵמָה וְאֶחָד מַעְשַׂר דָּגָן,
phrases.english: one is animal tithe and one is grain tithe.
From the place where you bring up grain tithe,
you bring up animal tithe;

phrases.aramaic: וּמִמְּקוֹם שֶׁאִי אַתָּה מַעֲלֶה מַעְשַׂר דָּגָן
phrases.english: and from a place where you do not bring up grain tithe,
you do not bring up animal tithe!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבי עקיבא's derivation from the פסוק quoted in step 7.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי עקיבא limits מעשר בהמה to ארץ ישראל, against the משנה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The plural "מעשרותיכם," which links animal tithe to grain tithe.

steps.title: Our משנה can follow רבי עקיבא: sacrifice versus sanctity
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says our משנה can agree with רבי עקיבא. The ברייתא speaks about bringing the animal to be sacrificed, and our משנה speaks about the animal becoming holy.
steps.simpleTranslation: You can even say our משנה follows רבי עקיבא. There, he means it is not brought to be sacrificed. Here, the משנה means it still becomes holy.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from steps 6–8 by showing that רבי עקיבא and our משנה are talking about two different things.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא's ruling, that animal tithe comes only from ארץ ישראל, is about whether it is offered on the מזבח. Our משנה, which applies animal tithe in חוץ לארץ, is about whether the tenth animal becomes holy. So there is no contradiction: in חוץ לארץ the animal becomes holy but is not sacrificed.

keyTerms.meaning: You can even say (a way to keep the original view)
To be offered as a sacrifice

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רבי עקיבא holds that animal tithe in חוץ לארץ means nothing. According to this answer, it still becomes holy. It just isn't brought to the מקדש.

phrases.english: You can even say it follows Rabbi Akiva:
here (the baraita) is about being sacrificed, here (the mishna) is about being consecrated.
phrases.notes: Two different questions, so the two sources do not clash.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge that our משנה does not follow רבי עקיבא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי עקיבא holds there is no animal tithe at all outside ארץ ישראל.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי עקיבא only excludes sacrificing it. Sanctity still applies in חוץ לארץ.

steps.title: The verse רבי עקיבא cites supports this reading
steps.stepSummary: The wording of the ברייתא backs up the answer, because רבי עקיבא quotes "וַהֲבֵאתֶם שָׁמָּה", a verse about bringing to the מקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: The wording also shows this. He took his source from "and you shall bring there." Learn from this that he is talking about bringing it to be offered.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings support for its answer from the exact verse רבי עקיבא used.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא's verse speaks about bringing offerings "there", meaning to ירושלים. So his limitation is about bringing and sacrificing the animal, not about whether it becomes holy. This confirms the split made in step 9.

keyTerms.meaning: The wording is also precise (it supports this)
"And you shall bring there" (to the place of the מקדש)

phrases.english: The wording is also precise,
since he takes as his source
"and you shall bring there." Learn from this.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer of step 9 from the ברייתא's own wording.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי עקיבא's ruling concerns sacrificing, not sanctity.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The verse "וַהֲבֵאתֶם שָׁמָּה" that he cites.

steps.title: If it is never sacrificed, what is its holiness for?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what purpose holiness serves if the animal in חוץ לארץ can never be offered.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, since it is not offered, why is it holy?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the new answer: holiness with no possible sacrifice seems pointless.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, an animal becomes holy so that it can be offered. If tithe animals in חוץ לארץ are never brought, the גמרא asks what practical difference their holiness makes.

phrases.english: If so,
since it is not sacrificed, why is it consecrated?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the distinction just made in step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that tithe in חוץ לארץ becomes holy though it is not sacrificed.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Holiness without any possible sacrifice seems to have no purpose.

steps.title: Its holiness means it is eaten only once blemished
steps.stepSummary: The holiness has a real effect: the owner may eat the animal only after it develops a מום.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is holy so that it is eaten by its owner only when it has a blemish.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the holiness makes a practical difference in how the animal may be eaten.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the animal is holy, the owner cannot simply eat it like ordinary meat. He must wait until it gets a מום, and then he may eat it. So the holiness is meaningful even without a sacrifice.

keyTerms.meaning: A blemish that disqualifies an animal from the altar

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי עקיבא, animal tithe in חוץ לארץ becomes holy but is not sacrificed. The owner eats it only after it gets a מום.

phrases.english: To be eaten in its blemished state by the owner.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifying the practical effect of the holiness
steps.terutzMaskana: Holiness restricts eating until the animal has a מום.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה: with or without the Temple
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next phrase of the משנה: animal tithe applies both when the בית המקדש stands and when it does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: animal tithe applies in the presence of the Temple and not in the presence of the Temple.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic by quoting the משנה's words. This is a setup for the challenge that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says that animal tithe is not limited to Temple times. Quoting this ruling prepares the question of why it is not practiced in our day.

keyTerms.meaning: When the בית המקדש does not stand
The tithe of animals (every tenth animal is holy)

phrases.english: (The mishna said:) in the presence of the Temple and not in the presence of the Temple.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to a new phrase in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Animal tithe applies even without the בית המקדש.

steps.title: Then why don't we tithe animals today?
steps.stepSummary: If animal tithe applies without the Temple, it should apply nowadays too, but people do not practice it.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, it should apply even today!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה's ruling by pointing to the current practice of not tithing animals.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's rule logically leads to animal tithe being required today. Since in practice it is not done, the גמרא needs to explain the gap.

phrases.english: If so, then even nowadays too (it should apply)!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the משנה quoted in step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that animal tithe applies without the Temple.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If it applies without the Temple, it should be practiced today, yet it is not.

steps.title: רב הונא: a rabbinic decree because of an orphan animal
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא explains that חז"ל made a גזירה not to tithe today because of a יתום, an animal whose mother died before it was born. Such an animal is exempt from the tithe.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is like רב הונא says: it is a decree because of an orphan animal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that animal tithe is stopped today by a rabbinic decree. The decree is out of concern that an exempt orphan animal would be included.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By Torah law, animal tithe could still apply today. But a יתום is exempt from the tithe, and people might wrongly include it in the count. So the רבנן stopped the practice.

keyTerms.meaning: An "orphan" animal whose mother died before its birth; exempt from מעשר בהמה

phrases.english: In accordance with Rav Huna, as Rav Huna said:
It is a decree on account of an orphan animal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers why animal tithe is not practiced today.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A rabbinic decree suspends the Torah-level obligation
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the Torah law applies, we should tithe today.
steps.terutzMaskana: The רבנן stopped it out of concern for a יתום being included.

steps.title: Then it should have been banned in Temple times too
steps.stepSummary: The worry about a יתום existed in Temple times as well, so the decree should have applied then too.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, then originally too it should not have been done!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב הונא: his concern is not unique to our time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An orphan animal could get mixed in just as easily when the בית המקדש stood. If that worry justifies stopping the tithe, it should have stopped it then too.

phrases.english: If so, then originally (when the Temple stood) too it should not (have been done)!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב הונא's reason from step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's גזירה because of a יתום.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same concern existed in Temple times, yet they did tithe then.

steps.title: In Temple times an announcement solved the problem
steps.stepSummary: Back then, the concern could be removed by publicly announcing that a יתום is exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it was possible to fix it with an announcement.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that in Temple times there was a simple fix: a public announcement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If everyone is told that an orphan animal is exempt, nobody will wrongly include it. So in Temple times there was no need for a decree.

phrases.english: Rather, it was possible (to solve it) through an announcement.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers why there was no decree in Temple times.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The יתום concern should have banned tithing in Temple times.
steps.terutzMaskana: Then, an announcement removed the concern.

steps.title: Then an announcement should work today too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: if an announcement solved the problem then, it should solve it now as well.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here too, it should be possible with an announcement!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer again: an announcement could be made today too. The next step answers this challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer in step 17 seems to work just as well today, which would undo רב הונא's reason. The גמרא does not find a difference between then and now. Instead, it drops רב הונא's reason and gives a new one in the next step.

phrases.english: Here too (nowadays), it is possible through an announcement!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 17 by applying its solution to today.
steps.kashyaTarget: The distinction between Temple times and nowadays.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If an announcement worked then, it should work now, so there is no reason for the גזירה.

steps.title: רבה's new reason: fear of a mishap
steps.stepSummary: רבה drops the יתום explanation. He says we do not tithe animals nowadays because of a risk of תקלה, meaning someone might misuse a holy animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבה said: it is because of a possible mishap (תקלה).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a brand-new answer to the question from Step 14. This replaces רב הונא's יתום answer, which was just knocked down.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without the בית המקדש, a tithe animal cannot be brought as a קרבן. It would sit around as a holy animal for a long time. Someone might shear it or work with it, which is forbidden with holy animals, so חז"ל stopped tithing altogether.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (rejects the earlier answer and gives a new one)
A mishap, a stumbling block: the risk that someone misuses something holy

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up רבה (with a ה at the end) with רבא (with an א). This statement belongs to רבה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the reason the rest of the סוגיא builds on: holy animals that cannot be offered today are a danger.

phrases.english: Rather, Rabba said:
phrases.notes: אֶלָּא shows that the יתום answer has been dropped.

phrases.english: It is because of a possible mishap,
phrases.notes: The mishap is misusing a holy animal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the יתום answer after it was rejected in Step 18
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought the decree was because of the יתום problem
steps.terutzMaskana: The decree is because a holy animal that cannot be offered may lead to misuse

steps.title: Asking for a source that we worry about a mishap
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how we know that חז"ל are concerned about תקלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And from where can you say that we are concerned about a mishap?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a source for רבה's idea. This sets up the proof that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה's reason is a new idea. Before accepting it, the גמרא wants to show that חז"ל really made rules to avoid a תקלה.

keyTerms.meaning: From where can you say this? (asking for a source)

phrases.english: And from where can you say
phrases.notes: This is the usual way the גמרא asks for a source.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for support for רבה's reason
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source showing that חז"ל worry about misuse of holy things nowadays

steps.title: Proof from a teaching: nothing may be made holy nowadays
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that nowadays one may not consecrate, give an ערכין pledge, or make a חרם. If someone did, the item must be destroyed.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: One may not consecrate, nor make an ערכין pledge, nor make a חרם nowadays. If one did consecrate, make an ערכין pledge, or make a חרם: an animal must be destroyed. Fruit, clothing and vessels must be left to rot. Money and metal vessels must be taken to the Dead Sea.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source it asked for. The source shows that חז"ל would rather destroy holy things than risk them being misused.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without a בית המקדש, holy items have no proper use. They might be used for everyday purposes by mistake, which is a serious sin. Destroying these items only makes sense because of a fear of תקלה, so רבה's idea has a firm source.

keyTerms.meaning: Consecrate: give something to the בית המקדש
Make an ערכין pledge: promise a set value of a person to the בית המקדש
Make a חרם: dedicate something as a special holy gift
Nowadays, when there is no בית המקדש
The Dead Sea, where things are thrown so no one can use them

steps.whyThisMatters: This ruling, which also appears in עבודה זרה, is the basic source for the rule that one should not make things holy nowadays.

phrases.english: As we learned: One may not consecrate,
nor make a valuation pledge, nor make a dedication (חרם)
in the present time.
And if he did consecrate, make a valuation pledge, or dedicate,
an animal must be destroyed,
produce, clothing and vessels must be left to rot,
money and metal vessels:
phrases.notes: These items never rot, so a different method is needed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 20's request for a source
steps.raayaObject: רבה's claim that חז"ל worry about תקלה nowadays
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא forbidding making things holy nowadays and requiring destruction of anything made holy

steps.title: How an animal is destroyed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains what "destroying" an animal means: locking it in a room until it dies by itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is 'destroying'? He locks the door in front of it, and it dies on its own.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the word תיעקר means in practice and answers right away. This explains a word from the source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The animal is not slaughtered directly. Instead it is shut away until it dies by itself, so it is gone and no one can misuse it. This shows how far חז"ל went to avoid a תקלה.

phrases.english: And what counts as destroying?
He locks the door in front of it
and it dies on its own.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the word תיעקר from the ברייתא
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What it means in practice to destroy a holy animal
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Lock it in a room until it dies by itself

steps.title: Then a firstborn should not become holy either
steps.stepSummary: If we worry about תקלה, then a בכור should also be prevented from becoming holy.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, a firstborn animal should also not become holy!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבה's reasoning. If misuse of a holy animal is the worry, the same worry applies to a בכור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nowadays a בכור also cannot be offered. It must wait until it gets a blemish, and in the meantime it could be misused. So the danger of תקלה should lead us to prevent בכור holiness too.

keyTerms.meaning: If so (the logic leads to a hard result)
Firstborn male of a kosher animal, which is automatically holy

phrases.english: If so,
a firstborn should also not become holy!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי בְּכוֹר נָמֵי לָא לִיקְדֹּשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבה's תקלה reason by applying it to בכור
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same risk of misuse exists with a בכור, but we do nothing to stop it from becoming holy

steps.title: A firstborn becomes holy by itself
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: a בכור's holiness does not depend on us, because it becomes holy at birth.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does the matter of a firstborn depend on us? It is holy from the womb!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the challenge from Step 23. Tithing is something we choose to do, but a בכור becomes holy automatically.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חז"ל can tell people not to tithe, because tithing needs a person's action. A בכור needs no action at all; it is holy the moment it is born. So there seems to be nothing to forbid.

keyTerms.meaning: Holy from the womb, automatically at birth

phrases.english: Does the matter of a firstborn depend on us?
It is holy from the womb!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the challenge of Step 23
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The comparison between בכור and מעשר בהמה
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: בכור becomes holy without any human action, so there is nothing for חז"ל to forbid

steps.title: The real question: sell part to a non-Jew
steps.stepSummary: The questioner explains his real point. We could sell the ears of the unborn animals to a non-Jew, so they never become holy at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what he means: Let us sell their ears to non-Jews, so that they do not become holy in the first place!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the challenge from Step 23 more sharply. The challenge was never about stopping holiness at birth, but about preventing it ahead of time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An animal partly owned by a non-Jew does not become a בכור. Selling even a small part, like the ears, before birth would stop the holiness, and with it the risk of תקלה. So if חז"ל worried about תקלה, they should have required this, and the question stands for now.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what he means (explains the earlier statement)
Let us sell (give ownership of) them
From the start / in the first place

steps.confusionAlert: The ears are not really the point. Any shared ownership with a non-Jew, even of a small part, stops the animal from becoming a בכור.

phrases.english: This is what he means:
Let us sell their ears to non-Jews,
so that they do not become holy in the first place!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Restates the challenge of Step 23 in a way that avoids the rejection in Step 24
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: We have a way to prevent בכור holiness ahead of time, and we do not use it, so the worry about תקלה seems not to be a real concern
